title: The tzimtzum and the reshimu: the teacher's one point, the soul in the body, the blueprint and the thrown stone
overview:
Chapter 12 explains the first *tzimtzum*, the first that relates to our *hishtalshelus*, and the *reshimu* left after it. They must be understood in detail and felt, because that is the key to true unity with *Atzmus Ein Sof*: seeing that everything, even the highest revelations and *Moshiach* itself, is like nothing before Him, a check to be cashed, so that a person wants only G-d Himself.

All the *meshalim* of the *tzimtzum* come to one point: the light is hidden in itself so that a little can shine. A teacher boils a deep idea down to one point for a small student, yet forgets nothing, and the short way holds it all, as the *Mishna* holds the *Gemara*. The soul holds back to live in a body, yet feels everything the body feels and loses nothing when a limb is lost.

The *reshimu* is an impression: nothing of the original is left, yet all of it can be drawn out. A blueprint, a mnemonic, a thrown stone, a hand sign and the moving fingers of a writer each hide it more, and the last points ahead to the *Kav*.

terms.gloss: contraction: the light hidden in itself so that only a little shines; not literal, since nothing is missing
an impression: the original is completely gone, not a residue, yet what was there can be figured out and drawn out of it
self-sacrifice: giving up anything, physical or even spiritual, to connect to G-d Himself
the days of old: here the middos as they are preceded in the essence before the tzimtzum, which is not bound by them
a vessel for a vessel: revealed not directly but indirectly, like an engraving in a diamond pressed into wax
He engraved an engraving: a double engraving, the letters estimated in Kadmon
the whole debate and reasoning behind a ruling, which the one who says it short still knows
the short way: the summary or the Mishna's short din, which includes all the length
the receiver; the student who is not comparable to the teacher
the form of man: the soul's spiritual form, hovering over the body and making it go the way it should
an impression or mark; here the craftsman's blueprint, a shorthand from which the whole building can be made

sections.title: Why the tzimtzum must be understood in depth: before Him everything is as nothing
sections.summary: The first *tzimtzum* and its *reshimu* look simple, but they have many details and must be felt, not only understood, because they are the key to unity with *Atzmus Ein Sof*: seeing that everything, even the whole *hishtalshelus* and the revelations of *Moshiach*, is like nothing before Him.

phrases.en: And now, we have to understand
the idea of this first *tzimtzum*.
as well as the *reshimu* that is left, the impression that's left after this first *tzimtzum*.

blocks.text: **And now, we have to understand the idea of this first tzimtzum** (contraction), for which he will give a *mashal* (analogy), and with it **the reshimu that is left**: the impression left after this first *tzimtzum*.

Really, this is not the first *tzimtzum*. Before it come *tzimtzumim* between *Echad* (one) and *Kadmon* (preceding), between *Yachid* (singular) and *Echad*, between the *etzem* (essence) and *Yachid*, and even one from G-d Himself to the idea of *Atzmus* (G-d's essence) at all. This one is called the first because it is the first main one that relates to our *hishtalshelus* (the chain of descent).

phrases.en: even though that is known to people that are familiar with *Kabbala* and *Chassidus*,
nevertheless there's many details to the *tzimtzum* and the *reshimu*.

blocks.text: Everybody familiar with *Kabbala* and *Chassidus* knows about the *tzimtzum* and the *reshimu*; **nevertheless there's many details to the tzimtzum and the reshimu**. It is not as simple as people think: "Ah, the light was there, and then He took it out, and now there was an empty place."

phrases.en: you have to really cultivate a deep sensitivity for these ideas.

phrases.he: כי זהו עיקר היחוד האמיתי בעצמות אור אין סוף
phrases.en: because this, a proper understanding and really feeling the idea of the *tzimtzum* and *reshimu*, is the main thing, the main requisite for a true unification with *Atzmus Ein Sof*.
how everything is like nothing to Him.

phrases.he: גם בבחינת כללות כל ההשתלשלות דקו וכו'
phrases.en: even the whole totality of the *hishtalshelus* of the *Kav*

blocks.text: There are two reasons to study these details. The subject is very complex; and *lehaamik hadaas*, **you have to really cultivate a deep sensitivity for these ideas**, a deep feeling and recognition for them. You should really feel it, not just understand it intellectually.

Really understanding and feeling the *tzimtzum* and *reshimu* **is the main thing, the main requisite for a true unification with Atzmus Ein Sof**: seeing everything in the world, yourself included, as a revelation of G-d. For that you must realize *kula kamei k'la chashiv*, **how everything is like nothing to Him**. It is just G-d revealing Himself; the world looks like it is here because He hides everything He is except this little thing, a little nothing.
Another side of *kula kamei k'la chashiv*: everything in the *hishtalshelus* is less than what is before it, and less to the point where it is infinitesimal, like nothing.

You say, "Ah, look at this. I have this great, yummy, triple chocolate fudge cake. It's so good. Mmm." No, that's like nothing. G-d has infinite fudge chocolate cake, not just triple fudge. The *geshmak* (relish) and the pleasure in it come from a little *nitzotz* (spark), a little revelation of G-d in it. The full revelation would be so pleasurable that the soul would leave the body: "At least right now, without proper lenses and stuff."
blocks.title: Triple chocolate fudge cake

blocks.text: So when you look at anything, like a table, G-d is hiding everything He can do except for this table. And making a table is like nothing compared to what He could really do.

By the way, "just a little interesting side": *nigleh* (the revealed Torah) also explains *kula kamei k'la chashiv*. In *Ein Yaakov* the word is *k'la*, like *la*. And *la* is the name of the stuff that comes out from the sun, a dust it makes scraping against its orbit or something; its background buzz is why during the day you cannot hear things from as far away. "So you know, that's interesting."

It is the *mashal* of light: everything in the world is like light from the sun, with no *metzius* (existence) of its own. Even where you see it as its own *metzius*, it is like photons, the least physical of the physical things, whose whole existence is to reveal the light coming from the essence.
blocks.title: The la that comes from the sun

blocks.text: That is *nigleh*; in *Chassidus* there are two things. *Kula kamei k'la chashiv* says the world is a *metzius*, but it is like nothing. *Ein od milvado* (there is nothing besides Him) says there is no world. It is not a contradiction: the world is *mamash* a *metzius*, because G-d made it as a revelation of Himself. Only the revelation you see in the *hishtalshelus* is a little token example, like nothing compared to the full revelation of G-d, if you would appreciate it.

**Even the whole totality of the hishtalshelus of the Kav** (the line of light) is like nothing: our world with all the spiritual worlds, the lower and upper *Gan Eden* (paradise), and higher, *Atzilus*, *Adam Kadmon*, and even the revelations of *Moshiach*.

Yes. What we want is not the external things of *Moshiach*, peace and tranquility and prosperity, and not even the revelations of *memalei kol almin* and *sovev kol almin* (the light that fills all worlds and the light that encompasses them). "We want that when *Moshiach* comes, then we're going to see G-d Himself."
blocks.question: Even Moshiach is like nothing? The whole thing we want is Moshiach!

blocks.text: This is what we say on *Shabbos*: *Ein aroch lecha Hashem Elokeinu ba'olam hazeh*... In this world, in *Gan Eden*, in the time of *Moshiach* and in the World to Come, it is all worthless without G-d. *Efes bilt'cha*: it is nothing without You.

When a person realizes that everything he sees, even the greatest spiritual revelations, is only a little token, symbolic thing, whose point is for you to see the *atzmus u'mahus* (the essence) behind it, the revelation of G-d, he will not want the *tafel*, the secondary external thing. He will want the real thing behind it.

Otherwise it is like a guy who gives you a check. You do not want the check; you want the money in the bank behind it. Even a dollar bill: the paper and the artwork are worth something, but you want what it is backed by, much more than the paper is worth. A big guy's signature alone is worth something, but if he writes you a million dollar check, you want the money.

So the world is like a check. The main thing is to cash it, to get what is in the bank; the world is just the symbolic way of giving it over. Then you will not want the world as its own thing; it is like nothing. "So G-d gave us a check for infinite stuff, and we should, you know, cash it."
blocks.title: The check and the money in the bank

sections.title: Directing the will to the Essence alone: what is there for me in the heavens?
sections.summary: Understanding the *tzimtzum* lets a person aim his will, with *mesirus nefesh*, at *Atzmus Ein Sof* alone. Every revelation, even *sovev* before the *tzimtzum*, the heavens of the heavens, cannot contain Him, not even as a vessel for a vessel.

phrases.en: Until a person will be able to straighten out his desire

phrases.he: במסירת נפש לעצמות אור אין סוף לבדו
phrases.en: that he'll self-sacrifice just for the *Atzmus Ein Sof* itself

blocks.text: **Until a person will be able to straighten out his desire**: when he properly understands the *hishtalshelus* and the *tzimtzum*, he will look past other things to what is really important, and want that. That is *mesirus nefesh* (self-sacrifice), **that he'll self-sacrifice just for the Atzmus Ein Sof itself**: give up anything physical, even spiritual, to connect to G-d Himself, since everything else is meaningless in itself. "If you have that, you have everything."

The famous *mashal*: the king lets people into his treasure chamber to take whatever they want, but sets up booths around it with food, music and other distractions. People start partying, figure they have so much time, and then it is too late. So *Hashem* sets up all these revelations, and a person dazzled by the physical and the spiritual things goes off after them.
blocks.title: The king's treasure chamber and the booths

blocks.text: *Lechaven* means to direct it straight, like a laser pointer, or the sights on a gun that you get aimed and aligned. When a person understands the *tzimtzum*, he is able to aim his *ratzon* (will) properly.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב אתה הוא יהו״ה לבדך,
phrases.en: like it says, you are *Hashem* alone,
that You, etc.

blocks.text: **Like it says, you are Hashem alone**: not only is there nothing else of value, there is nothing else at all. Then **that You, etc.**: the verse goes on, that You made the heavens and the earth and everything in them, and that everything bows to You. What He made is just part of His revelation, not its own thing; everything bowing to You means everything is *batel* (nullified) to *Hashem*.

phrases.en: And this is what it means: the King that is exalted alone, that He's above everything.

phrases.he: בחינת מלכות דאין סוף שלפני הצמצום
phrases.en: this is the idea of *Malchus* of *Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*,

phrases.he: שמתנשא גם מימות עולם דאדם קדמון,
phrases.en: which is exalted over the days of the world of *Adam Kadmon*, meaning that it transcends even the limitations of *Adam Kadmon*,
this *Malchus* of *Ein Sof* is called *yemei kedem*.

blocks.text: **And this is what it means: the King that is exalted alone**: we call G-d the King who is above everything. **This is the idea of Malchus of Ein Sof before the tzimtzum.**

It **is exalted over the days of the world of Adam Kadmon**, transcending even its limitations. *Adam Kadmon* is the general image of the final goal of the whole *hishtalshelus*, the way it will be when *Moshiach* comes. *Hashem* is above even that; He just chose it to represent the way we will connect to Him, and our *avoda* (divine service) is to do that.

**This Malchus of Ein Sof is called yemei kedem** (the days of old). Usually that name is for *Adam Kadmon*, but here he calls *Adam Kadmon* *yemos olam*: the days of the world, the regular limitations of the *hishtalshelus* or of any level. *Yemei kedem* is those *middos* (attributes) as they are preceded in the *etzem*, which is not bound by them.
*Yemei kedem*: "that's like in the good old days, where, you know, he had to walk uphill both ways to school and stuff like that," where it is impossible.
So here he is talking about *Malchus*, the *middos*, the way they are in the *Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*, which, as was said at the end of chapter 11, is called *yemei kedem*.

phrases.en: the heavens
the heavens represents the general *sovev*, the general encompassing light that's after the *tzimtzum*.
and the heavens of the heavens,
which is before the *tzimtzum*, which means the lights of the *tehiru ila'a*,
they cannot contain You.
it's not even a vessel for a vessel,
like it says that He engraved an engraving in the higher purity

blocks.text: This is **the heavens** of the verse "The heavens and the heavens of the heavens cannot contain You": **the heavens represents the general sovev, the general encompassing light that's after the tzimtzum**, the light that includes the whole *hishtalshelus*.

**And the heavens of the heavens, which is before the tzimtzum**, the lights of the *tehiru ila'a* (the upper purity): **they cannot contain You.** Even the lights before the *tzimtzum* do not capture G-d's essence. He is way higher than everything.

**It's not even a vessel for a vessel, like it says that He engraved an engraving in the higher purity.** What is a vessel for a vessel, an engraving for an engraving?

You engrave letters into a diamond, but you cannot read them; there is not enough contrast. So you press the diamond into wax, and in the wax you see the letters that were in the diamond. So too, the letters engraved in *Kadmon*, in the *glif glifu* (He engraved an engraving), are still too fine to see; that is why it is a double engraving. After the *tzimtzum* they are stamped out as on wax and you can see them. That relationship is a *kli l'kli* (a vessel for a vessel), an engraving for an engraving.
blocks.title: The engraved diamond pressed into wax

blocks.text: So what is not revealed directly is revealed indirectly. But G-d Himself is not revealed even indirectly, even as a vessel for a vessel: nothing captures Him, even as a representation of what He really is.

He is higher than everything. On one hand nothing can reveal Him; on the other, when He chooses to reveal Himself in something, the whole essence is there. But nothing captures Him inherently: "either you have it or you don't." You have to connect to Him directly. Understanding even the highest revelations will not capture Him.

phrases.en: And like it says, what is there for me in the heavens?

phrases.he: שהוא גם בחינת סובב הכללי שלפני הצמצום
phrases.en: which includes even the general *sovev* that's before the *tzimtzum*,
which is called the heavens of the heavens.
And with You I desire nothing on the earth,

phrases.he: בבחינת קו וחוט בחינת ממלא הכללי כו'
phrases.en: the earth represents *memalei*, the way that G-d is revealed not in a transcending way, but in an individualized way in *hishtalshelus*, in the *hishtalshelus* of the *kav v'chut*.

blocks.text: **And like it says, what is there for me in the heavens?** That **includes even the general sovev that's before the tzimtzum, which is called the heavens of the heavens.** **And with You I desire nothing on the earth**: **the earth represents memalei** (filling), G-d revealed in an individualized, measured way, in the *kav v'chut* (the line and the thread), in *chachma* and *bina* and the rest. Once you have G-d, you have everything; without Him it is all worthless.

Early on the *Alter Rebbe* would fall into *dveikus* (cleaving to G-d), roll on the floor and say, "I don't want Your *Gan Eden*, I don't want Your World to Come, I only want You alone."

Before his passing he said he knew the revelations of both *Gan Edens*, of *chachma* of *Atzilus*, even the essential ones, where *chachma* equals *Asiya*, "but I give myself over with my whole power of *mesirus nefesh*" so that *Hashem* should hear every Jew's prayer like a *tzaddik gamur*'s (a perfectly righteous man) on *Rosh Hashana*.
blocks.title: The Alter Rebbe: I only want You alone

blocks.text: "I don't know," says Rabbi Walters, "maybe" the point is that the highest *mesirus nefesh* is as *HaYom Yom* says: it is better to love whom *Hashem* loves than even to love *Hashem*. Wanting to be connected to G-d is still kind of selfish; better is to want Him to be good to His people.

sections.title: The tzimtzum in one point: the light hidden in itself so that a little can shine
sections.summary: There are many *meshalim* for the *tzimtzum*, but they all come to one point: so that the infinite light can be drawn down in a measured way, as a *Kav*, G-d hid the revelation of Himself within Himself and let only a little shine, making a quantum leap from infinite to finite.

phrases.he: והנה יש כמה אופנים במשלים שונים להשכיל ביאור ענין הצמצום הנקרא מקום פנוי
phrases.en: There are many different types and ways of *meshalim* to be able to understand, to get a concept of the *tzimtzum*, which is called the empty place,
as is known to somebody that goes into these things in depth.

blocks.text: Now the *tzimtzum*, and then the *reshimu*. **There are many different types and ways of meshalim** (analogies) **to be able to understand, to get a concept of the tzimtzum, which is called the empty place**, the *makom panui*, **as is known to somebody that goes into these things in depth.**
Why so many? In general the *tzimtzum* is a very simple *mashal*, but to really understand it properly, the deeper the idea, the more *meshalim* you need, and in different ways.

phrases.en: but the general idea of the *tzimtzum* comes to one main point.

phrases.he: והוא כדי שיוכל להיות אור אין סוף בבחינת השפעה בצמצום בבחינת קו,
phrases.en: that in order for the infinite light, the revelation of G-d, to be brought out in a limited way, in a measured, limited way, which is the idea of the *Kav*,

phrases.he: הוצרך לצמצם עצמות אורו שישאר בהעלם בעצמותו
phrases.en: G-d hid *atzmus oro*, He hid the revelation of Himself, so that it should remain hidden within Himself,
and it shouldn't all shine,
just a little bit of it,

phrases.he: כדי שיהיה אחר כך המשכות האור בדילוג הערך
phrases.en: And through this, that *Hashem* hides His *atzmus or* and just brings out a little bit, there could be a jump, a quantum leap in its *erech*, in its quality, in its degree.

blocks.text: With all these different *meshalim*, **the general idea of the tzimtzum comes to one main point**: **that in order for the infinite light, the revelation of G-d, to be brought out in a limited way, in a measured, limited way, which is the idea of the Kav** (the line), **G-d hid** *atzmus oro*, the essence of His light: **He hid the revelation of Himself, so that it should remain hidden within Himself.**

**And it shouldn't all shine, just a little bit of it.** By hiding the essence of His light and bringing out a little bit, **there could be a jump, a quantum leap in its erech** (measure), **in its quality, in its degree**: from an infinite thing to a finite thing, from a creator to a creation.

sections.title: The first mashal: the teacher boils a deep idea down to one point, and nothing is missing
sections.summary: A teacher hides the depth of his understanding and gives the student one point, but he has not forgotten the rest, and the short way includes all of it, as the *Mishna* includes the whole *Gemara*. So the *tzimtzum* is not literal: from the teacher's side and from the student's, it is all there.

phrases.he: והרי זה כמשל אור שכל עמוק ורחב שבעצמות המשפיע
phrases.en: This is like a *mashal* of a deep and broad subject within a teacher's brain,

phrases.he: שכדי שיומשך ממנו למקבל הבלתי ערך אליו,
phrases.en: in order for him to bring this idea over, to teach it to a student that is much lower than him, it's not comparable to him,

phrases.he: הוצרך המשפיע להעלים בעצמו כל עומק השגתו,
phrases.en: The teacher has to hide within himself the whole depth of his understanding.

phrases.he: ולא ישאר רק בחינת רושם, כנקודה א',
phrases.en: So he has to hide everything and only leave an impression like one little point of what he wants to say,
from the whole depth and the whole breadth with all the details,

blocks.text: **This is like a mashal of a deep and broad subject within a teacher's brain.** **In order for him to bring this idea over, to teach it to a student that is much lower than him**, **the teacher has to hide within himself the whole depth of his understanding**, or the student will be confused. **So he has to hide everything and only leave an impression like one little point** of what he wants to explain **from the whole depth and the whole breadth with all the details.**

A big math genius knows math in all its depth and all its branches, the breadth: fractions, irrational numbers, trigonometry, calculus, "and all kinds of things that I don't know about at all. You know, they do like differential equations or something."

Now he teaches a two-year-old. He starts with one little point: one and one is two. But that is still abstract; not complicated, but abstract. What is one and one? So he makes it simpler: one fishy and one fishy are two fishies. "But we're not up to there": so far he has only brought it down to one little point.
blocks.title: The math genius and the little kid

blocks.text: Einstein wrote a book on relativity that he says anybody can understand, with an analogy of somebody bouncing a ball on a train: the person on the train sees it go straight up and down, the person on the ground next to the train sees it go forward in little rainbows. He takes this whole thing and makes it much simpler.
blocks.title: Einstein's ball on the train

phrases.en: it's not like the depth and the width and the breadth of the idea go away completely.

phrases.he: רק כמו השונה בדרך קצרה, שכל העומק ורוחב הפלפול ישנו בשכלו,
phrases.en: it's not like he forgot about the rest of the details, but rather it's like somebody that's just saying something over in short, like a summary, that he has the whole depth and the whole width in his head.

phrases.he: רק שהוא נכלל לפי שעה בהעלם עצמותו
phrases.en: just that it's now hidden within himself.
right now he's just saying the point in short.

blocks.text: Distilling it to one point does not make the depth and breadth go away. **It's not like he forgot about the rest of the details, but rather it's like somebody that's just saying something over in short, like a summary, that he has the whole depth and the whole width in his head**, the whole *pilpul* (debate), **just that it's now hidden within himself.** He knows it, but he is not thinking about it, because **right now he's just saying the point in short**: the *kitzur*.

You ask somebody the *halacha* and he tells you the bottom line. Ask him why, and he starts: "Oh, well, it's a whole thing": the verses, the *Gemara*'s dispute and how they ruled, the *Rishonim*, the *Shulchan Aruch*, the *Shach* and the *Taz*, "and finally we get to the *halacha*." He knows the whole *pilpul*, but he just tells you, "You can eat the chicken. It's kosher."
blocks.title: You can eat the chicken

phrases.en: but if you're a *talmid chacham* or something, and you want to know, and you ask him, then he'll explain, and the more you know, the more he'll expand and explain more to you, all the way back to the way that he understands it.

phrases.he: רק בשביל שיובן למקבל דרך זה הקצר, מעלים גם בעצמו לפי שעה
phrases.en: just that in order for the recipient to understand this short way, he has to make it short, and even for himself he just focuses on the point.
as is explained elsewhere at length.

blocks.text: But if you are a *talmid chacham* (a Torah scholar) and ask, "Why did you rule that way?", he will explain, and the more you know, the more he will expand, all the way back to the way he understands it. **Just that in order for the recipient to understand this short way**, **he has to make it short, and even for himself he just focuses on the point.**

Back in Europe you took a chicken to the *shochet* (slaughterer), then to the *dayan* (rabbinic judge) to check that it was kosher, then home to salt it, so chickens were always coming to the *Rav*. Some lady asks if hers is kosher, and he starts, "Well, the *Shach* says like this, and the *Taz* said like that." She does not want to know all that; she will be confused.
blocks.title: The chicken brought to the Rav

sensitivity.reason: The questioner is "some lady" who does not want the sources and "will be confused" by them; read alone it can sound condescending to women.
sensitivity.publishable: Back in Europe you took a chicken to the *shochet* (slaughterer), then to the *dayan* (rabbinic judge) to check that it was kosher, then home to salt it, so chickens were always coming to the *Rav*. Somebody asks if his is kosher, and the *Rav* starts, "Well, the *Shach* says like this, and the *Taz* said like that." He does not want to know all that; he will be confused.

blocks.text: To be a good *Rav*, you have to just say the *halacha* clearly, as if that's it. Even with a lenient ruling, do not make them feel it is *b'dieved* (acceptable only after the fact); it is *l'chatchila* (the proper way from the start): "That's it, that's what you're supposed to do." If they are poor and cannot, so that's it, that's good.

Some people are not so good with that. You ask them a *halacha* and they say, "Well, ah, not so simple, there's this, there's that," and you come away not knowing what the *halacha* is. "That's not what you need to hear."
So too, give the student all this explanation and he will not even get the point; you have to tell him the point in very simple terms. **As is explained elsewhere at length.**

phrases.he: 13 ומה שנשאר כמו נקודה, שהוא דרך קצרה,
phrases.en: and this that the idea is left like a little point, that's just a very short point,
it's not a true and complete *tzimtzum*.
like somebody that completely hides the idea,
then it would be totally missing to the *mekabel*.

phrases.he: אלא הענין הוא שכולל בדרך קצר זה כל האריכות,
phrases.en: So the idea is that when the teacher says this short, simple explanation for the student, the whole long idea is all hidden within that short explanation.
And he's not missing a point, and not even a half a point,

blocks.text: **And this that the idea is left like a little point, that's just a very short point**, like little short notes you make for yourself, or the short way you tell the student: **it's not a true and complete tzimtzum.**

That would be **like somebody that completely hides the idea; then it would be totally missing to the mekabel** (the receiver): the teacher decides, "This is too complicated for you, I'm not going to teach it to you," or that it is a secret. Then the student gets nothing. Here the teacher is trying to explain the idea, but cannot tell it the way he himself understands it, so he makes it short.

**So the idea is that when the teacher says this short, simple explanation for the student, the whole long idea is all hidden within that short explanation.** **And he's not missing a point, and not even a half a point**: not even the minute details. The student is really getting the full explanation.

phrases.he: כמו שכלול בדין הקצר שבמשנה כל האריכות הפלפול שבגמרא
phrases.en: just like how in the short *din* in the *Mishna* is included the whole *pilpul* in the *Gemara*.

phrases.he: וכמו שלא נעלם ליודע כל הפלפול גם בשעה ששונה לעצמו דרך קיצור
phrases.en: and just like for the teacher that knows the whole *pilpul*, it's not missing to him even when he teaches it in a short way,

phrases.he: שנמצא שידיעתו באריכות מקפת בהעלם כל התגלות הקיצור
phrases.en: So it comes out that his knowledge of the whole long explanation of the *Gemara* encompasses in a hidden way the whole revealed short explanation of the *Mishna*.

phrases.he: ולא שנסתלק לגמרי כשכחה וכהאי גוונא כו'
phrases.en: And it's not like it totally went away, that he forgot it.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב ביאור זה באריכות במקום אחר.

blocks.text: **Just like how in the short din** (law) **in the Mishna is included the whole pilpul in the Gemara.** Analyze the *Mishna* and you can extract the *Gemara* from it, because Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, writing it, knew the whole *pilpul* of why we say it, the main thing of the *Gemara*.

Not exactly our *Gemara*, with its *Amoraim*, but its points, why the *halacha* is this way or that way, Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi knew. He chose the cases, the wording and the order carefully. Each *din* teaches a general rule, a principle; analyze them, compare and contrast them, look at the order and the examples, and you get *chiddushim* (new insights), the common denominator and the difference, and you can extrapolate the reasoning and reconstruct the whole *Gemara*. That is what the *Amoraim* did: taught by their teachers how to learn the *Mishna*, they extracted the whole *Gemara* from it again and wrote it down.

**And just like for the teacher that knows the whole pilpul, it's not missing to him even when he teaches it in a short way**: when Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi looked at the *Mishna*, his notes, he saw the whole *pilpul* of the *Gemara* there. **So it comes out that his knowledge of the whole long explanation of the Gemara encompasses in a hidden way the whole revealed short explanation of the Mishna. And it's not like it totally went away, that he forgot it.**

So too the student is really getting the full explanation; he just does not realize it yet. As he studies and develops his mind, he will appreciate more and more of what he was taught, until he sees everything like the teacher.

So the main theme of the *mashal* of the teacher and the student: you need the *tzimtzum*, but the *tzimtzum* is not literal. The teacher hides most of his intellect and gives over one little point, yet the whole understanding did not really go away, both from the teacher's point of view and from the student's.

From the teacher's side there are two things. He did not forget it, so if you ask him, he can explain it to you. And when he looks at the short explanation, he sees the whole thing in it: tell him that short explanation and he would understand everything, without your having to explain it.

The student too gets only one short explanation but is not missing the rest: as soon as he is ready and has a question, he asks and gets it. And it is there not only in the teacher but in the little explanation itself: even if the teacher goes away, by studying what he was told he can get everything, because it was all there.

So it is there in the teacher's mind and in the explanation; the student, with his small mind, just does not appreciate it yet. As he develops, he will see everything like the teacher. That is the first, main *mashal* for the *tzimtzum*.

sections.title: The second mashal: the soul holds back to live in the body, yet stays whole
sections.summary: To become the life of the body the soul hides most of what it can do, since the two are not comparable. Yet the whole soul is bound to that small light and feels what the body feels, like a plant tied to the earth's power of growth; and when a limb is lost, nothing is lost to the soul.

phrases.en: the second main type of *mashal*.
the consciousness of the soul in the body.

phrases.he: גם כן עולה על דרך הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: it also comes to a similar conclusion, similar point as the previous *mashal*.

blocks.text: Now **the second main type of mashal.** After the teacher and the student, the second main *mashal* for the *tzimtzum* is **the consciousness of the soul in the body**, and **it also comes to a similar conclusion, similar point as the previous mashal.**

phrases.he: והוא בהיות שכדי שישתנה מחיי רוחניים שבעצם הנפש לחיי בשר, הוצרך להיות בחינת העלם וכיווץ האור של הנפש בתחלה
phrases.en: in order for the soul to come into the body, the soul has to hide its full potential,
because there is no comparison between the two.

blocks.text: As the teacher has to hide the full depth of his understanding, which is too much for the student, so **in order for the soul to come into the body, the soul has to hide its full potential**. The soul can do much more than the body: see much more than it sees and understand much more than it understands.

In a dream, or a hallucination, a person sees all kinds of things. But when the soul comes into the body we tell it, "Hey, you know, easy there. We want you to only see what the eyes see."

Sitting in class, instead of listening to the teacher or even seeing him, your imagination wanders off and you are in a whole other world. That is just from the eye to the brain; from the soul it would be even more unlimited. So we want the soul to keep quiet and see only what the eyes see when light hits them, "or else there's no point in being in the body."
blocks.title: Daydreaming in class

blocks.text: So to come into the body the soul says, "Okay, I'm going to put aside everything that I can do," and waits: it sees only when light hits the eye and hears only when air hits the ear. It does this automatically, because it wants to come into the body. A person who really wants to can sometimes go out of the body a little, but then he will not see and hear.

Once the Rebbe Rashab was saying a *maamar* (a Chassidic discourse) and people were making noise in the side room. Since his whole desire was to teach *Chassidus*, he unconsciously shut off the ear facing that room. Later they realized he could not hear out of that ear, figured out it was from that, and he turned it back on. His soul had decided it did not want to be in the ear anymore, so it left.
blocks.title: The Rebbe Rashab's ear

blocks.text: Or in *dveikus* the soul goes up and is not receptive; it sees higher things, kind of like a dream. Higher still is *nevua* (prophecy). A prophet totally loses his physical senses during a prophecy, except Moshe, who stood face to face as if talking to a regular person. The regular prophets were called crazy people: they would fall on the ground, unable to see or hear anything around them, because the soul was going out of the body a little. So to come into the body, the soul has to limit itself and be revealed only according to the body.
**Because there is no comparison between the two.** The body is too small to hold the real light of the soul, so the soul has to hide its true potential, at least at first.

phrases.en: nevertheless,
The soul is affected by what happens to the body, the soul itself.

phrases.he: אם כן גם אור הגשמת החיות תתחבר ונקשר אל אור עצמותה הרוחני
phrases.en: Even though the light of the soul is coming into the physical life, when a person sees something or feels something, it is connected to and tied to the essential light of the soul.

phrases.he: כצמיחה גשמית שנקשר בכח הצומח הרוחני כו'
phrases.en: Like the physical growth of a plant, that even though there's just a little plant, it's connected to the spiritual power of growth.

blocks.text: **Nevertheless, the soul is affected by what happens to the body, the soul itself.** It is not that a little ray of the soul comes into the body while the soul stays aloof: the ray comes in, but the whole soul is attached to it.

**Even though the light of the soul is coming into the physical life**, the seeing and feeling, **it is connected to and tied to the essential light of the soul.** So if you hit somebody, his soul feels the pain; hurt or insult him, and it can hurt him to the core of his being. It is not some little biological impulse; his whole soul feels it. So too with pleasure: the whole soul gets excited.

**Like the physical growth of a plant, that even though there's just a little plant, it's connected to the spiritual power of growth.** "It's like very metaphorical": a plant has a thin little stem in the ground, and the earth is a huge, massive potential for growth. The stem siphons out one little drop of it, and even that is filtered by the roots to take only what this plant can use; different plants use different nutrients, which is why they rotate crops. It brings out one little possibility, according to the seed and the DNA. But disconnect it from the source and it will not grow anymore: it is connected constantly to the whole source.
blocks.title: The thin stem and the whole earth

blocks.text: In the same way, if the whole soul were not in the body, the body could not see or hear or feel. You need the soul to be there, or else the person would not be alive.

phrases.en: but when a limb of the body is, G-d forbid, cut off,

phrases.he: לא יחסר באור וחיות רוחניות של אבר זה
phrases.en: it will not detract from the light and the spiritual life force, spiritual consciousness of this limb.
and the proof is
from a blind person that is able to give birth to someone that can see.
as is known,

blocks.text: That is the one side: we see that on the one hand it is only a little, only a *tzimtzum*, only a little bit of it, and yet the whole essence is there. Now the other side.

**But when a limb of the body is, G-d forbid, cut off, it will not detract from the light and the spiritual life force, spiritual consciousness of this limb.** The whole soul is connected to the body, but it is not trapped there: hurting the body will not hurt the soul.

**And the proof is from a blind person that is able to give birth to someone that can see.** If his soul lacked the power of sight, he could not give it over, because reproduction makes something like you, with a certain minimal variation: people give birth to people, animals to animals, plants to plants. If losing an eye, G-d forbid, meant the soul lost the power of sight, it would be as if you took one power out of the soul, and from then on there would be a new species of people that do not see.

But that is not the way it is. Even physically, in the spiritual side of the physical, the DNA, the letters, the potential of sight, are still there; it just has to be brought out into actuality in a healthy eye.

Even when the DNA gets messed up: "I don't know exactly how it works," says Rabbi Walters, but they tried to make wingless fruit flies with genetic engineering and breeding. The wings got smaller and more defective, closer and closer to none, and then after a few times the next generations would revert to perfectly healthy flies. Something in the way it is set up, the soul, forces it to follow a certain form and keeps it from departing from it too much. **As is known.**
blocks.title: The wingless fruit flies

phrases.he: אין זה רק שהרוחניות הוא בהעלם,
phrases.en: Because the spiritual power is still there in a hidden way.

phrases.he: וישנו במציאותו, חופף על חיות הגשמי שבגוף
phrases.en: and it exists in its totality, in its perfect state, hovering over the physical life force of the body.
it's called the form of man.

phrases.he: והיינו על דרך הנזכר לעיל בידיעה שבהעלם כו'
phrases.en: and this is like the knowledge of the teacher that is hidden in his short explanation.
and all of this is explained elsewhere at length.

blocks.text: That is **because the spiritual power is still there in a hidden way, and it exists in its totality, in its perfect state, hovering over the physical life force of the body.** **It's called the form of man**, the *tzelem*: a spiritual form that hovers over the body and makes it go the way it is supposed to go.

You even see this a little with a phantom limb: someone who loses a limb can still feel it sometimes, since for the consciousness in his brain the hand is there. That is still somewhat physical; as far as the soul goes, as in a dream, for sure he has the whole thing.

**And this is like the knowledge of the teacher that is hidden in his short explanation.** As there it is all there from the teacher's and the student's point of view, so the soul still has the whole life force, still the power of sight or whatever was lost; even the body has it, in the DNA, only hidden.

More than that: as the whole depth is in the short explanation, the body could reveal the whole light of the soul. It just needs to be refined until it is able to.
At the time of *techiyas hameisim* (the resurrection of the dead), when *Moshiach* comes, the body will be refined enough to reveal the whole light of the soul.

That, by the way, is why people do not live forever now. It is painful for the soul to be in the body, unable to express its whole essence there, so after a while it gets sick of it and starts to pull out, and the body goes down until the person dies.

But if the whole soul came into the body, with its whole *ratzon* to be there, it could regenerate the whole body from one little part, the way it will be with the *luz* bone at *techiyas hameisim*. You see it with a child, who develops very quickly from one little cell, two little cells.
blocks.title: Why people don't live forever

blocks.text: **And all of this is explained elsewhere at length.** Those are the two main *meshalim*. Now he says quickly that there are also a few other *meshalim* like this.

So far, two main *meshalim* for the *tzimtzum*. A teacher teaching children a deep idea puts aside the way he understands it and leaves a simple explanation, like the *Mishna* to the *Gemara*. He does not forget it and sees its whole depth in the explanation; the student receives it all too, only he does not appreciate what he is seeing. And the soul in the body: its essence is connected to the body, so a person is affected by what happens to it, yet an injury to the body does not detract from the soul. "So now we're going to explain the *reshimu*."
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 29 opens by summing up both meshalim of the tzimtzum (lines 17-40) before it reads line 44; placed here, at the end of the second mashal.

sections.title: More meshalim: the power of movement and the genius in one idea
sections.summary: The power of movement contracts into one movement and the genius into one idea, yet each stays bound to its source: the body moves only with the soul, and in one idea you see the whole genius. One-way: the source gives life to the detail, but the detail does not capture the source.

phrases.he: וכן כח התנועה הרוחניות כשבאה בתנועת הגשם, מתצמצמת בעצמותה כו'
phrases.en: So too, when you move, the spiritual power of movement has to be limited severely in order to come and make a particular movement.

phrases.he: ועם כל זה התנועה גשמית מחוברת ומקושרת בתנועה הרוחנית
phrases.en: Nevertheless, the physical movement has to be connected to the spiritual movement, or else it won't move.

blocks.text: **So too, when you move, the spiritual power of movement has to be limited severely in order to come and make a particular movement.** The whole power is infinite, able to make so many movements, and it comes into just one.

**Nevertheless, the physical movement has to be connected to the spiritual movement, or else it won't move.** "Like I said, dead dogs don't bark." Without the whole essence of the soul, the body could not move.

But the movement does not capture the soul. Moving the body will not make it alive: "Like Frankenstein wouldn't work." Electricity through the body can make it move, but that is just the physical side; it gives no life. The whole essence of the soul connects to the body, but it is not trapped there.

It is a one-way thing, "like a square is a rectangle, but a rectangle isn't a square." With the soul, the body can move; without it, it cannot. But having the body, even moving it, does not capture the life of the soul.

phrases.en: and so too with other types of *meshalim*,

phrases.he: כמו ענין התחכמות שכל פרטי מכח המשכיל שלו ששורה עליו בהעלם כו'.
phrases.en: like when a person comes up with a particular idea, the person's whole genius is really expressed in that one idea.

blocks.text: **And so too with other types of meshalim, like when a person comes up with a particular idea, the person's whole genius is really expressed in that one idea.** Yet the idea does not capture his genius: without it he could not have come up with it, but understanding what he said will not make you a genius like him.

Only he could come up with it, but to do so he has to limit his genius to one very limited way. He still has his whole power of intellect and knows he could come up with any idea. And looking at this one idea, you see not just the idea but the genius, and that he could come up with any idea.

Not only that: really study what he wrote or said, and it starts to make you think like him, until you can come up with ideas like he can. That is *osios haRav* (the teacher's letters): the letters themselves, not the idea but the way he said it, hide his way of thinking.

By the way, that is what is said about the *Mishna*. The way they thought was so much greater than ours, really a G-dly intellect, not humanly possible. So what do you do? If you study *Mishnayos* a hundred times, the angel of the *Mishna* comes down and teaches it to you. Going over the letters and the ideas again and again sets up your brain to think like the *Mishnayos*; every review reinforces those patterns, until you get the way the *Tannaim* thought, and then you understand it.

So with anything: learn a *maamar* sixty times and you get the *etzem*: "Then you *chap atzmus*" (grasp the essence).

sections.title: The reshimu: an impression, like a blueprint or a mnemonic, from which the whole can be drawn
sections.summary: A *reshimu* is an impression: the original is gone, nothing of the light is left, yet what was there can be drawn out of it. The craftsman's marks and a sign made to remember hide the intellect more than the *Mishna* hides the *Gemara*, since the *Mishna* still speaks of the same thing.

phrases.en: however, in order to understand the *reshimu*,
that the idea of a *reshimu*, of an impression, implies that everything was removed to be hidden,

phrases.he: ולא נשאר מהכל רק רושם כו'
phrases.en: and nothing is left, just an impression, but none of the original light is left.

blocks.text: **However, in order to understand the reshimu**: *reshimu* literally means an impression. In those detective movies a guy writes a phone number on a pad and rips the page off; the other guy rubs a pencil over the pad and sees it. People think *reshimu* means a residue; it doesn't. The original is completely gone, but you can figure out what was there from the impression it left, like a footprint or a fingerprint.
The idea of a *reshimu*, of an impression, **implies that everything was removed to be hidden, and nothing is left, just an impression, but none of the original light is left.**

phrases.he: הוא מובן יותר מענינים משלים אחרים,
phrases.en: so the *reshimu* is better understood by different *meshalim* than we said until now.
for example, a blueprint.

phrases.he: שיוכל לעשות הבנין בקיצור קו זה שברושם, שכולל כל אריכות המעשה בקיצור רושם זה
phrases.en: You're able to take the blueprint, and you're able to build the whole thing.

blocks.text: **So the reshimu is better understood by different meshalim than we said until now.** "Till now we gave like five *meshalim* for the *tzimtzum*, now we're going to give five for the *reshimu*."

The *roshem* (mark) the craftsman makes is, **for example, a blueprint. You're able to take the blueprint, and you're able to build the whole thing**, a skyscraper or a house, just by following it. Any craftsman first draws a design: a new *aron kodesh* (ark) in woodwork, or a silversmith's *Kiddush* cups.
blocks.title: The craftsman's blueprint

blocks.text: Not just a drawing; that would be different. A blueprint is a few lines, symbols and marks, a shorthand for the dimensions. A normal person would not understand it, but if you know how to read it, you can build the entire thing from it. So the first *mashal* is a craftsman's notes: no instructions, no picture, no manifest explanation at all. You would have to know how to do it.

As he will say in a moment, the *Mishna* still relates to what the *Gemara* spoke about. The *Gemara* talks about a cow that gores somebody else's cow: who pays whom, what if it was the first time, the second, the third, what if it was in the sun. The *Mishna* talks about that too, only with much less. Anybody who learns *Mishnayos* gets a general knowledge of Jewish law; he may not appreciate the real depth, why these cases were chosen and not others, but even without explanation he understands what is going on.

A blueprint, if nobody explains it to you, you will not understand. There the intellect, how to build the thing, is there but completely hidden.

phrases.he: או כמו שעושה לזכרון הנקרא אות
phrases.en: Or like somebody that makes a sign to help him remember,

phrases.he: שאין האות ענין שייך אל עצם הענין,
phrases.en: the sign has nothing to do with the actual thing you're trying to remember,
it's just to help you remember.
like it says in the *Gemara*, you should make mnemonics for yourself,

blocks.text: **Or like somebody that makes a sign to help him remember**, like tying a string around his finger. The string has nothing to do with what he wants to remember; nobody can look at it and figure out what that was.

**The sign has nothing to do with the actual thing you're trying to remember, it's just to help you remember**, **like it says in the Gemara, you should make mnemonics for yourself.** Like "Roy G. Biv" for the colors of the rainbow: it is hinted there, which is more than a string on the finger, yet nobody would figure it out by looking. Or for the planets: "My very eager mother just served us nine juicy pickles." The mnemonic alone tells you nothing; once you know, it helps you remember.
blocks.title: Roy G. Biv and the nine juicy pickles

phrases.he: וזהו בחינת העלם יותר מקיצור ההלכה ששונה וכולל בו הכל
phrases.en: this is more of a concealment of the intellect than the teacher that summarizes the law, like in the *Mishna*, that he includes everything in a very short way,

phrases.he: שעל כל פנים שייך ענין הקיצור אל האריכות
phrases.en: because there, the short explanation of the *Mishna*, for example, still relates directly to the long explanation.

blocks.text: **This is more of a concealment of the intellect than the teacher that summarizes the law, like in the Mishna, that he includes everything in a very short way, because there, the short explanation of the Mishna, for example, still relates directly to the long explanation.** You see the relevance. So these are the first two *meshalim* of the *reshimu*.

sections.title: Deeper concealments: the thrown stone, the hand sign and the writing finger
sections.summary: In the thrown stone the force is severed from the thrower yet carries his whole power; in a hand sign and in the moving fingers of a writer the intellect is hidden further still, until it reappears on the paper. All the *meshalim* of the *reshimu* make one point: the essence is hidden, yet all of it is included in the impression.

phrases.en: there's another type of *mashal* for the *reshimu*,

phrases.he: שהוא מורה ענין הצמצום וההעלם הרבה יותר
phrases.en: which reveals a much deeper type of a concealment within the *reshimu*, a different aspect of the *reshimu*.
this is like somebody that throws a stone.

phrases.he: שכח המוליך אותו נבדל מן העצם
phrases.en: that the force that's carrying the stone is severed from him.

blocks.text: **There's another type of mashal for the reshimu, which reveals a much deeper type of a concealment within the reshimu, a different aspect of the reshimu.** **This is like somebody that throws a stone**: **the force that's carrying the stone is severed from him.**

In class a kid throws a paper airplane or a spitball, then sits like everybody else, and you don't know who did it, because once he throws it the force he put into it is severed from him. He does not have to move his arm; he can sit there looking in his book. The object no longer shows the person, and the person can rest: they are separate.
blocks.title: The spitball in class

phrases.he: ועם כל זה כל כח התנועה מלובש בו בהעלם
phrases.en: but nevertheless, even though you don't see the connection anymore between the person and the stone or whatever it was he threw, his entire power of movement is in there; that's what's moving it.

phrases.he: אך שהוא בריחוק נבדל ביותר מכחו העצמי שבידו
phrases.en: but the force that's in the stone is very distant and it's completely separate from the force of his hand.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן כח התנועה עצמה שמניעה בעצמו בגשם שמלובש בגלוי בגשם ביותר כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: On the other hand, if somebody actually holds something and moves it, then you see the connection between the person's power of movement and the thing that he's moving.

blocks.text: **But nevertheless, even though you don't see the connection anymore between the person and the stone or whatever it was he threw, his entire power of movement is in there; that's what's moving it**: his strength, his desire, really his whole essence. That is why he is responsible: if the stone damages property, or kills somebody, he could actually be killed. His soul is held accountable for this stone.

**But the force that's in the stone is very distant and it's completely separate from the force of his hand.** **On the other hand, if somebody actually holds something and moves it, then you see the connection between the person's power of movement and the thing that he's moving**; it is much more manifest. Throwing leaves just an impression of your force in the thing, a kind of *reshimu*, and you can go back to rest.

It is the same with all of these. The architect puts the instructions for building the building into the blueprint and can walk away; somebody else can build it. "If they know how to read a blueprint, the guy can die, nobody cares, they can build it."

phrases.he: ויש בחינת העלם יותר גם מזה,
phrases.en: the *reshimu* has even more of a concealment than this,
this *mashal* is similar to the *mashal* of the mnemonic.

phrases.he: והוא כמו הרומז בידו לאיזה שכל עמוק ביותר
phrases.en: this is like a person that hints with a hand motion to a very deep idea.
the physical movement is totally detached from the idea.

phrases.he: ועם כל זה מבין השכל מתוכו כו'
phrases.en: Nevertheless, even though it's just a motion, just a hand movement, a person understands the intellect within it if you know what it represents.

blocks.text: And **the reshimu has even more of a concealment than this**, which we see from a different *mashal*; **this mashal is similar to the mashal of the mnemonic.**

**This is like a person that hints with a hand motion to a very deep idea.** The whole hippie philosophy is represented by these two fingers, and it is just a hand movement. Or when the Rebbe would go like this, a whole thing was understood: not being *nifal* (swayed), going against everything and doing what you have to do with determination. "Well, what's that?" It is just a motion.
blocks.title: The peace sign and the Rebbe's gesture

blocks.text: **The physical movement is totally detached from the idea.** Somebody once connected his intellect to this motion; now nobody has to put content into it. It has already been thrown: "Nobody's like creatively coming up with this peace sign." **Nevertheless, even though it's just a motion, just a hand movement**, "So what's a guy waving fingers in my face?", **a person understands the intellect within it, if you know what it represents.**

phrases.en: and even more than this,

phrases.he: העלם אור השכל בתנועת האצבע בכתיבתו אותו

phrases.en: explained elsewhere at length.

blocks.text: **And even more than this** is the concealment of the light of the intellect in the movement of the finger when one writes. You can be writing the deepest ideas, and your hand is just moving your fingers like this. Neither you nor anyone watching sees the intellect in those motions; you see it only when it comes out again on the paper: oh, there was an intellect. It just passes through.

Really this book itself is the *mashal* for all of them. The Mitteler Rebbe took G-d and the whole *hishtalshelus*, made it short and simple, just 80 pages with little *meshalim*, wrote it down and threw it: from Russia to America, 200 years into the future, and it landed here. We don't see the Mitteler Rebbe walking around anymore, yet it is his book and he is responsible for how we understand it; that is why at the beginning he asks to be forgiven for any mistakes. "It's like he's sitting behind the book and teaching it to us."
blocks.title: The book thrown two hundred years

phrases.he: והכל עולה לסגנון א' הנזכר לעיל

blocks.text: **But all of these meshalim of the reshimu are really the same general point: that the essence remains hidden, that the original light is gone, is hidden completely**; **but even though it's hidden, it's all included within this reshimu or this point.** You do not see it at all, and yet it is all there, because you can pull it all out.

He gives five *meshalim*, or six, and they are not for the same thing; they never use the same *mashal* for the same thing. Why so many is explained in a *maamar* in *Ateres*, by the Rebbe Rashab, and in a letter of the Rebbe about it. The main idea is that it keeps being more hidden.

All the *meshalim* show how hidden the *reshimu* is, with two main points. One: the intellect is completely hidden, and yet you can pull it out. Two: it becomes separate, far away. It is detached from the essence, so you do not see the connection; and it is a *shinui hamahus* (a change of nature), no longer looking like intellect: just a motion, a mnemonic, a blueprint's few squiggles with no instructions for building a building in sight. And it can be thrown: the original person can leave, and it is completely self-sufficient, so to speak.

This last *mashal*, the writing, "I think," says Rabbi Walters, introduces the *Kav*, as the *mashal* of growth at the end of 13 seems to introduce the *tzimtzum*'s relation to the light before it. Chapter 14 will ask how the light can come out of the *reshimu* if it is completely hidden there like a point. In writing, the intellect is hidden down to a point in the moving fingers, with no revelation of intellect at all, and on the paper it is revealed again. "And we'll discuss how that works later."

reviewQuestions.question: Why is this tzimtzum called the first, when there are tzimtzumim before it?
How do kula kamei k'la chashiv and ein od milvado differ, and why is there no contradiction between them?
What does it mean that even the heavens of the heavens are not a vessel for a vessel, and what is the mashal of the diamond and the wax?
In the mashal of the teacher and the student, in what ways is the whole idea still there, from the teacher's side and from the student's?
How does a blind parent's seeing child show that the soul loses nothing when the body is injured?
Why is the blueprint a greater concealment than the Mishna, and the writing finger greater still?

notes.text: Line 62 is not marked as read by the alignment, but he reads it at tape 29 w2362-2391 ("והא כל אלו לסגנון אחד אופן הנ״ל"); it is joined to line 63 in one passage, whose phrase for line 62 cites that stretch.

Several phrases cite his rendering inside the explanation rather than right after the reading: line 3 ("you have to really cultivate a deep sensitivity"), line 31 (the soul hides its full potential), line 38 ("Because the spiritual power is still there"), line 41 and line 47 (the blueprint). Lines 14 (its last kaf-vav), 22 (kaf-vav), 29 ("as is explained elsewhere"), 61 (the middle of the line) and the end of 10 and 63 are read without English and have none.
The explanation of k'la in Ein Yaakov (the la, a dust from the sun scraping its orbit that drowns out sound by day) is kept as he gives it, loosely and from memory; he gives no exact source.
He says "Till now we gave like five meshalim for the tzimtzum, now we're going to give five for the reshimu", and at the end "he gives five meshalim ... or six". Kept as said.

"Just like at the end of 13 he gives the mashal of the growth": the mashal of the growth is line 35 of this chapter (12). The chapter file's line 23 begins with a stray "13", probably a page or edition number; he may be counting by that. Kept as said.

Sources he cites from memory: HaYom Yom (better to love whom Hashem loves than to love Hashem), the angel of the Mishna after studying Mishnayos a hundred times, a maamar learned sixty times, a maamar of the Rebbe Rashab in Ateres and a letter of the Rebbe on why there are several meshalim. Reported as given.
The fruit fly experiment (wingless flies reverting to normal) is his recollection, which he hedges ("I don't know exactly how it works"); kept as said, unflagged since it is not advice.

Sensitivity: one block is flagged, the story of the lady who brings a chicken to the Rav and "will be confused" (women; replace, with the questioner made neutral). Considered and left unflagged: the aside on rabbis who answer "not so simple, there's this, there's that" (unnamed, a remark on how to answer), "the whole hippie philosophy is represented by these two fingers" (descriptive, not disparaging), regular prophets "called like crazy people", and why people do not live forever (a Chassidic explanation, not health advice). A public editor may want to look at the hippie line and the Rav aside.
Tape 24 has a lighter, more colloquial voice than the others ("yummy, triple chocolate fudge cake"); the catalog gives it as his class, and it is treated as such.

Review: three phrases were trimmed to his English for their own Hebrew only. Line 9 ("vezehu hashamayim") now has only "the heavens" (his rendering inside the verse he quotes), not the whole verse; line 31 drops "because the soul can really do a lot more than the body can do", which is his explanation, not the line; line 48 drops his example "like ties a string around his finger". The blocks keep those words unbolded.
